title: Gradient Descent & Learning Rates
description: Navigate optimization landscapes. Compare Batch, Stochastic (SGD), and Mini-Batch Gradient Descent and tune learning rates.

slides.title: Gradient Descent Intuition 🏔️
slides.content:
# The Foggy Mountain Analogy

Imagine standing blindfolded on a foggy mountainside, wanting to descend to the deepest valley floor.

At each step, you feel the slope of the ground beneath your boots (the **gradient**) and take a step in the direction of steepest descent.

### The Parameter Update Rule:
$$\mathbf{w} \leftarrow \mathbf{w} - \alpha \nabla_{\mathbf{w}} \mathcal{L}$$

* **$\nabla_{\mathbf{w}} \mathcal{L}$ (Gradient Vector):** Points in the direction of steepest *ascent* in loss.
* **Minus Sign ($-$):** We step in the opposite direction to *minimize* error.
* **$\alpha$ (Learning Rate):** The step size taken downhill on each update iteration.

slides.title: Comparing Gradient Descent Flavors ⚖️
slides.content:
# Batch vs Stochastic vs Mini-Batch

| Gradient Descent Variant | Samples per Update Step | Computational Efficiency | Trajectory Smoothness | Memory Footprint |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Batch Gradient Descent** | Entire dataset ($N$) | Poor on big data; cannot stream | Perfectly smooth; guaranteed convergence | Prohibitive (must hold all data in GPU memory) |
| **Stochastic GD (SGD)** | Exactly 1 sample | Frequent updates; escapes shallow traps | Highly noisy and erratic oscillations | Minimal (1 sample in memory) |
| **Mini-Batch GD** | Small batch (32, 64, 128, 256) | Highly optimized for SIMD/GPU tensor cores | Smooth convergence with healthy exploration | Tunable to fit GPU VRAM perfectly |

Mini-Batch Gradient Descent is the universal standard across modern deep learning.

quizData.question: What happens during neural network training if the learning rate alpha is set too large?

options.text: Training converges instantly to the global optimum
The parameter updates overshoot the valley and loss oscillates wildly or diverges toward infinity
All weight values freeze at exact zeros
The model reduces to a single-layer perceptron

quizData.explanation: An excessively high learning rate overshoots the minimum, causing catastrophic numerical divergence (loss exploding to NaN/infinity).

slides.title: Simulating Gradient Descent in Python 🐍
slides.content: Minimizing a quadratic loss function $f(w) = w^2 - 4w + 4$:
slides.codeSnippet:
w = 10.0 # starting far from minimum (w* = 2)
lr = 0.1

for step in range(25):
    grad = 2 * w - 4 # derivative df/dw
    w = w - lr * grad
    if step % 5 == 0:
        print(f'Step {step:2d} | Weight: {w:.4f} | Loss: {(w-2)**2:.6f}')

print(f'Final optimized weight: {w:.4f} (True optimum: 2.0)')

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: Learning Rate Schedules 🚀
slides.content:
## Learning Rate Warmup & Cosine Decay
Modern LLMs and vision models do not use a constant learning rate. They employ a **Cosine Annealing Schedule with Linear Warmup**:

1. **Warmup:** Start at 0 and ramp learning rate up over the first 2,000 steps to stabilize early gradient directions.
2. **Decay:** Smoothly decay the learning rate following a cosine curve down to 10% of maximum, settling into the sharpest minimums.
